first_impression.reaction: I searched 'wedding in crete' because Crete is on our list next to Puglia and nobody can tell me which end of the island we'd even be looking at. The opening gets straight to it: 'Crete is on your shortlist, and the questions now are practical ones: which month, which end of the island, and what moves the cost.' That is literally my three questions. No 'say I do in paradise', just east versus west in two sentences. Kept reading.

journey.quote: The east is resort country around Elounda and Agios Nikolaos; Rethymno and Chania in the west hold the harbour towns and smaller, more personal venues, with Heraklion in between.
journey.reaction: Useful straight away. 'Smaller, more personal' is the wedding we want, so I already know to look west first. I didn't know that ten seconds ago.

journey.quote: October brings milder days again, but rain days roughly treble compared with September at Heraklion.
journey.reaction: Real numbers from the actual weather service, not 'sunny all year'. The table is a lot to take in on my phone, but this sentence is the one I needed: September, not October. James will like the table.

journey.section: Venue season windows and ceremony times
journey.reaction: This is the kind of thing only someone who's done it would bother to mention. A 6.30pm ceremony changes the whole shape of the night and when the grandparents get to bed. I hadn't thought about it at all.

journey.section: The best time to get married in Crete
journey.quote: Greek official holidays include 25 March, 1 May, Easter Monday (which moves each year), 15 August, 28 October and 25 and 26 December.
journey.reaction: Good catch. I'd have picked a date and found out later that the registry office was closed.

journey.quote: Heatwaves are frequent over the summer months and can cause heat exhaustion and heat stroke, and many major tourist sites have little shade.
journey.reaction: Not what a sales page usually says. Honest. This paragraph is going to Mum and Dad, and it's pushing us away from July and August, which is fine.

journey.section: Choosing an area and a venue
journey.quote: Distances on Crete are real, and guests who land at one airport and stay at the other end will spend a good part of a day on the road.
journey.reaction: This is my exact worry about Nan and Pop. I didn't realise Crete had two airports at opposite ends. Glad someone said it plainly.

journey.section: Six venues from east to west
journey.quote: Not published: capacity or an exclusive-use option at St. Nicolas Bay, and capacity or a legal ceremony option at Caramel.
journey.reaction: I like being told what isn't known. But apart from Avra Imperial being big, I can't tell which of these six would actually take 60 to 90 guests. Guest count is the first thing I'd use to cross venues off, and the list doesn't let me do it.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Its civil package rate does not include the Municipal fees, and its Orthodox rate does not include the Metropolis fee, so those are charged on top.
journey.reaction: This is the hidden-cost stuff I'm scared of, named line by line. The whole cost section reads like a contract review. No numbers, but I know exactly what to ask about now.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Euphoria Resort at Kolymvari sells complete packages whose items are not interchangeable: a service not used brings no refund or alternative, and amendments or custom packages cost extra.
journey.reaction: That's the 'resort package' trap in one sentence. Useful to know before we fall in love with a brochure.

journey.quote: Put the same questions to each venue, and ask for the answers in writing.
journey.reaction: The ten questions are going into a shared doc with James tonight. Number 9, which year's terms apply, is one I'd never have asked.

journey.quote: Once on the island, most guests drive or take taxis.
journey.reaction: Half our guests are flying in from Australia, and our grandparents are not going to hire a car and drive Cretan mountain roads after a 24-hour trip. The section sets up the airport problem really well, then leaves arrival to taxis and 'ask your venue'. I still don't know who gets the older guests from the plane to the hotel.

journey.quote: Every notarial service needs an appointment, Monday to Friday from 9:00am to 12:30pm, though apostille and CNI documents can be sent by post, and legalised documents and CNIs are ready within two working days.
journey.reaction: I had to read this twice. Is this saying we might have to go to Athens for a CNI, or can we do it all by post from Sydney? The line earlier says DFAT can issue one in Australia too. I'm not sure which route applies to us.

journey.quote: Some couples marry legally at home and hold a symbolic ceremony on the island.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off, and probably what we'll end up doing given the 40-day registration. Good that it's said without making it sound second best.

journey.quote: For a legal wedding at the Elounda Collection, all documents must be issued within 3 months of the wedding date.
journey.reaction: The paperwork part of the timeline is precise, but it's all one east-coast resort group. If we go west to Chania, I don't know how much of this applies. And the venue and rooms steps have no time markers at all, so at 14 months out I still can't tell if we're early or late.

journey.section: Plan your Crete wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: 'One person, start to finish' is closer to what I want to hear than 'end-to-end'. Calm, not pushy. But it's the third time I've read 'confirms in writing before you commit' and the second 'time zone and AUD', so it starts to sound rehearsed.

unanswered_questions: Which of the six venues can actually hold 60 to 90 guests for a seated dinner?
Who arranges airport transfers for guests, especially older relatives who won't drive: the venue, Wedded Concierge, or us?
Is there a real Crete wedding you've planned, with the venue and date, that we can look at?
Does the CNI and paperwork process differ for a venue in Chania or Rethymno compared with the Elounda Collection?
How many months ahead do Crete venues usually need to be booked for a September date?
Who is physically at the venue on the wedding day: our Wedded Advisor, someone you're accountable for, or the hotel's coordinator?

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
turn_offs_found.why: None of the CTAs are pushy, which I appreciate. But this reassurance, or a near copy, appears after the venue list, after the costs and again at the end, and 'works in your time zone and quotes in AUD' appears twice. Repeated like that it reads like a script rather than a person talking, which makes me wonder how personal the service really is.

would_share_with: James (partner): the ten questions to ask every venue, and the month-by-month table so we can settle on May or September
Mum and Dad (contributing): the heat, wildfire and travel insurance paragraphs
Both sets of parents: the line about the two airports and the 180-minute drive, so they understand why the end of the island matters for the grandparents

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start planning with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-in-crete&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The tone is right and the article has earned some trust, but we haven't even picked between Crete and Italy yet. I'd want to read one or two more of your posts and see one real Crete wedding you've done, plus know who handles guest transfers and who's there on the day, before I hand over our details.

top_3_changes: In Six venues from east to west, give a guest capacity (or say 'not published') for each venue so a 60 to 90 guest couple can rule venues in or out at a glance.
In Getting there and getting around, say whether any named venue publishes guest or airport transfers (or that none do), rather than leaving arrival to driving and taxis.

Cut the repeated 'confirms in writing before you commit' and 'time zone and AUD' lines to one mention each, and add a short sentence in the timeline saying the paperwork steps shown are one venue group's and other venues differ.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie (planner_couple), using persona voice and concerns
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and VERIFY markers ignored
Title, business details and absent prices treated as not must-fix; no requests for sourcing lines, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: The venue list gives capacity for none of the six except Avra Imperial's 'very big wedding'. Does the crete-venues source pack hold published capacities the writer could add, or should each be marked 'not published'?
Guest transfers are a business detail (deferred) but the article section itself could state whether any named venue publishes transfer terms. Treat as should-fix or defer?

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'wedding in crete' during early destination research, about 14 months out; no other context was given.
Skimmed the month-by-month table and the six-venue list; read the cost, venue questions, airports and legal sections closely.
No prices appear by design, so the persona's 'vague pricing' turn-off was not raised.
Stock-photo turn-off not assessed because image slots are placeholders.
Family details (grandparents, parents contributing, Italy as an alternative) are persona colour, not brand facts.
The persona card is provisional (not CRM-calibrated).
